Fixes #9781.

issue_context.title: `gh workflow run --ref [ref]` ignoring `ref`
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

```bash
$ gh --version
gh version 2.59.0 (2024-10-16)
https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/tag/v2.59.0
```

Using the `ref` parameter does not seem to have any impact. A random-string `ref` gives no errors. A `ref` for an existing branch that has not yet been merged into the default branch reports 404 when trying to run a workflow that is new to that branch.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Create a new branch `foo`
2. Create a new workflow file `bar.yml` with `workflow_dispatch` and no other triggers
3. commit/push branch
4. `gh workflow run bar.yml --ref foo`

### Expected vs actual behavior

Expected: workflow `bar.yml` runs.
Actual: 404: Not found.

### Logs

Paste the activity from your command line. Redact if needed.

```bash
$ GH_DEBUG=true gh workflow run bar.yml --ref foo
[git remote -v]
[git config --get-regexp ^remote\..*\.gh-resolved$]
* Request at 2024-10-17 10:33:53.601824859 -0400 EDT m=+0.076128339
* Request to https://api.github.com/graphql
* Request took 309.171144ms
* Request at 2024-10-17 10:33:53.914645102 -0400 EDT m=+0.388948592
* Request to https://api.github.com/repos/[ORG]/[REPO]/actions/workflows/bar.yml
* Request took 134.922376ms
HTTP 404: Not Found (https://api.github.com/repos/.../bar.yml)
```
comments:
Hey @qodfathr,

So firstly, this is not a very useful error message (sorry!).

What's happening here is that `gh` is attempting to get information about the workflow from the `main` branch, and as you mention, it is not yet merged. This might seem like an oversight but actually, the platform itself **requires** the workflow to exist on the default branch for you to run it with `workflow_dispatch`.

https://docs.github.com/en/actions/writing-workflows/choosing-when-your-workflow-runs/events-that-trigger-workflows#workflow_dispatch

> Note: This event will only trigger a workflow run if the workflow file is on the default branch.

So although our error message is not very good here and we should fix it, what you're trying to do isn't possible at all anyway.

---

### Acceptance Criteria

**Given** I have at least one workflow on the default branch
**And Given** I have a new workflow `newworkflow.yml` on another branch `feature`
**When** I run `gh workflow run <newworkflow.yml> --ref feature`
**Then** I get an informative error message that says "the workflow newworkflow.yml not found on `<default branch>`, and workflows are required to exist on the default branch to be triggered by workflow_dispatch".

**Note**: At least one workflow is required on the default branch to avoid an earlier exit
Thank you, @williammartin , for the explanation! Understood.

That's interesting, the workaround seems to be:

> First, you need to temporarily add the pull_request trigger to the workflow, and create a PR with the workflow. This will cause it to run (and fail, if it needs inputs) and to appear on the Actions tab. Once it’s visible, you can remove the pull_request trigger.

Are you saying this doesn't work anymore?

To copy the error message from the AC:

```suggestion
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("workflow %s not found on the default branch, and workflows are required to exist on the default branch to be triggered by workflow_dispatch", workflowSelector)
```

Actually, this is possible with the [workaround](https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/9781#issuecomment-2631212474).
That's why I omitted this part as it does not correspond the existing UX (workaround).
By adding `push` and/or `pull_request` triggers in the non-default branch workflow, once it runs it's possible to remove other triggers and work with `workflow_dispatch` trigger using `gh workflow run`.

This workaround may need to be documented under #5268 and its link may be added here as part of the error.
Alternatively, the documentation may also be done here closing #5268.
Thoughts?
